Steven — validation replies on the 10-document invoice pilot.

FRAMING
I'll keep this at the level of what SIS should build — a crawlable list / database of supplier invoices that we can then query and use to validate invoices against our orders. I'm deliberately not handing over our internal day-to-day reconciliation formulas; those live with the purchasing team. The register just needs the fields that let the validation be done against it.

1. INTAKE + WHAT LANDS IN THE REGISTER
The purchasing intake is purchasing@sesameaccess.com. There is meant to be an identifier rule that categorises every inbound email carrying an invoice as an invoice, but it can miss cases because a supplier invoice is not always a clean attached PDF:
- A credit-card / payment-company supplier often issues no invoice — you get a receipt or an order confirmation instead.
- Sometimes the invoice is only a hyperlink to download, not an attachment.
- Fallback today: we screenshot the document or move it into an 'invoices to be processed' folder, then manually download and process it.

So there is a manual-groom step whenever the identifier can't produce a clean attached invoice. The register should accept a row in those cases (marked with how it was captured), not only perfect PDF-attachment invoices.

2. REGISTER MODEL (one row per document)
One purchase order can accrue several invoices AND several credit notes over its life, and it can get messy. So each document row needs:
- Supplier invoice / credit-note number and document type (Invoice / Credit Note / Receipt)
- Value (per document)
- A concept / context column so a row can say what it is doing (e.g. 2nd of 3 invoices for PO X; credit note against invoice Y; receipt from an auto-card supplier, not a real invoice)
- A date
- The order link (see matching below)

3. MATCHING (how the register connects to orders)
Match by mapping the supplier's order number or confirmation number against OUR order number, then resolve the invoice against that order. Do not match invoice-to-order purely on a value or a standalone supplier reference — the order/confirmation-number link is the reliable key.

4. VALIDATION ANCHOR
For any order, the set of documents against it should validate: sum of all invoice values MINUS sum of all credit notes for an order should reconcile to the order's Price Ex VAT held on the Asana task (itself the validated quote value). This is for validation/verification only — never auto-written back, never used to authorise. It flags 'this order looks fully invoiced / short / over / has an open credit note' for a human to look at.

5. TEN-SAMPLE DISPOSITIONS
- Exact Precision SA-49: invoice — register normally (has order context)
- 2x Amazon on PO 21592-10926: both register — the multiple-invoices-per-PO case; context column distinguishes
- KJN credit note 111772: credit note (negative/offset doc, not an invoice)
- BSI 97148247: invoice
- Apple 718180256797: likely receipt (auto-card supplier rarely invoices) — type Receipt
- Thameside / Midland Battery (scanned/no-text): capture row, mark scanned/no-text → manual entry, never blank-silent
- eBay seller statement: exclude as non-invoice, but log the exclusion with order context
- Deliberate duplicate: flag as duplicate in the daily view, never auto-merge

If any disposition is wrong, call it out and I'll correct.

6. EXCEPTIONS FOR THE DAILY REVIEW VIEW (none auto-actioned)
1. Missing PO/order match
2. Duplicate invoice number
3. Scanned / no-text (manual entry needed)
4. Context needed (multiple docs on one order unresolved)
5. Over-invoice / value-difference vs the order
6. Credit note present (offsets)
7. Receipt-not-invoice (so auto-card suppliers aren't miscounted)
8. Already-paid / awaiting-payment lifecycle status

SAFETY BOUNDARY
Validation only. No payment, approval, Sage, bank-detail change, source-doc move, or sign-off is requested or taken from this reply. Those remain human-controlled.
